title: Routine vs New Decisions Explained | Principles of Management Ep 22
description:
Chai Corner now has five outlets, and forty questions land on Ravi's desk every day. In this animated lesson Ravi learns that not every decision needs the boss, and sorts his questions into two bins.

You will learn Herbert Simon's two types of decisions (from The New Science of Management Decision, 1960): programmed decisions, which are routine, repetitive and made with rules and procedures at lower levels, and non-programmed decisions, which are new, unstructured and need judgment and creativity from top managers. We finish with a side-by-side comparison table.

This is Episode 22 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.

In this video:
0:00 Forty questions, all for Ravi
0:26 Herbert Simon's two types of decisions
0:40 Programmed decisions: rules and procedures
1:04 Non-programmed decisions: judgment and creativity
1:26 The sorting game
1:46 Side-by-side comparison
2:02 Quick check
2:17 Recap

Next episode: Rational Decision-Making.
